flattened_content:
Post Title: genuinely about to fail 3/5 of my classes
Post Body: yo midway thru the semester I randomly lost the urge to go to all my classes and now I'm about to fail them.

I know this is hilariously pathetic but please keep your laughter to yourself, I don't want to hear any criticism on how I let it get this bad I just need to get myself out of this pit.

Anyone who has been in a similar situation to me Is there anything I can do to maybe get an excusal for this semester instead of failing all my classes? I've already emailed all my professors whose classes I'm about to fail to try to appeal but I don't even know what to ask for, like do I ask for an extension? I don't really want to do that because I don't even trust myself to work on the stuff if I do. Especially because I myself don't really know what's going on I just stopped going to my classes

Or would it be better to just take the Fs take a semester to recuperate and idk fix whatever's going on and start anew? or am I being overly emotional? please speed i need this i don't know what's going on

EDIT: guys i talked to my professors and they were super understanding and gave me a path forward to pass. if anyone else sees this and is in a similar situation to me PLEASE swallow your pride and just talk to your professors and be open and honest. they are also people. and if they're mean then that's a them issue you don't deserve to just fail all your classes if you're willing to put in the work but you slipped up for a while

EDIT 2: and thank you so so much to everyone who took time out of their day to send advice or good wishes I've read all of it 🙏 got on some antidepressants and got a therapist so im feeling hopeful for the first time in months! i hope you all do well in your finals, stay strong, and know ur not alone in your struggle i've realized we're all going through it in some way 😭
Comment by umbral_sparrow: Go see someone in CAPS and see if they can help you with the emotional support. It was a good idea to message your professors because they’ll work with you. If all else fails withdraw from the semester and try again after you get some support for yourself. Don’t be hard on yourself either, it’s easy to get caught up in pressure from school performance, and just emotional turmoil in general. Idk what’s going on with your situation but you can work it out with help. Sending good thoughts your way op 

ETA: u/CameraActual8396 made a much better point about going off campus to find a better therapist you can get set up with and have a better chance of getting the help you need. If you have the insurance from Rutgers or are on your parents still this is the way, not CAPS!
Comment by Elemental_Love: I agree with this, and also, don’t worry about failing or dropping the classes. Take that stress off your mind completely. Either CAPS will know what to do and can help with that, or just let the Fs happen. It’s fine. You can retake the classes another time when you’re ready and the Fs will be dropped from your GPA and replaced with your new grades. Both the Fs and the new grades will show on your transcript, but only the new grades will be in your GPA. Don’t worry. I failed out of my first year due to just being kinda lost and having no one to ask. Now, I have my masters degree also from Rutgers and have been working in my career field for years. Drop all your worry, maintain the classes that you’re doing ok in(if you have that, if not it’s ok)and go to CAPS asap.
Comment by Standard-Bottle-3103: Taking a W is beyond better than accepting a F especially if your degree requires good grades the F stays on record just doesn’t affect gpa
Comment by Elemental_Love: True but I would think it’s past the deadline for a W. And if there’s one bad semester, but it’s reconciled later with good grades and a good gpa, I think that’s usually something future employers will regard as some personal circumstance which could be anything like a death in the family, stress, family struggles, or any other situation. Consistent low grades and low gpa would not be regarded in the same way as one bad semester. I and all three of my kids had circumstances that led us to earning an F or two at some point, after which we retook the classes and earned a good grade, and then the degree, and then everyone got on with their lives. I have my masters, and two of my kids are doing their masters now. Ws are the better option, but if it’s past the deadline, it’s still ok.
Comment by CameraActual8396: CAPS is not really the place to go tbh. They told me there's a month waiting list and even then, if your problem is deemed "too serious" they will refer you out. Like really. Plus it's only a few sessions. You would be better off finding an outside therapist.
Comment by umbral_sparrow: Very valid—OP if you took the insurance from Rutgers and didn’t waive it or are on your parents, USE IT and find someone who can help you.
Comment by CameraActual8396: Definitely-a lot of people don't realize this which is why I try to tell people. Better to try Rutgers EISS in Piscataway actually, they try to see someone within 24 hours and it's close to campus.
Comment by Rich_Yogurtcloset_23: Yes. If you're interested in CAPS, it's better to sign up for it earlier in the semester. There's usually a waitlist around exams/finals because a lot of people are stressed out around this time, and the therapists only schedule a meeting like once every two weeks. Even if OP signs up for CAPS now, it would only be like one therapy session at this point before the semester ends.
Comment by BeachgirlNJ0613: Yes! OP, take this advice. And go easy on yourself. You are young. It's not easy figuring all these things out. It may take time. Sounds like you are depressed. Please seek help through Rutgers Health. Or on your own. It's much easier to withdraw from classes with a medical excuse. Can you see a doctor and get a note? Truly, this is not the end of the world. But do something now to protect yourself. Sending love and support.
Comment by Miserable_Number9223: [https://scarlethub.rutgers.edu/registrar/registration/withdrawal-from-all-courses/](https://scarlethub.rutgers.edu/registrar/registration/withdrawal-from-all-courses/)
Comment by tkc324: First, it is a good sign that you are asking for help and trying to turn things around. Everyone slips up at some point. When I was in college, I rarely went to class and barely graduated. Looking back, I regret not taking school more seriously. At the time, all I wanted to do was spend time with friends and avoid lectures.

What is harder than going to class is struggling to land a decent job while watching friends move on to successful careers. Getting an F and assuming you can recover later is risky. I have seen too many people take that path and never finish school.

If things feel overwhelming, consider withdrawing and taking a semester off. Get a part time job, gain some perspective, and figure out what you really want. It is never too late to work hard and change direction, but you either do it now or you do it later in life. Trust me, it is much easier to do it while you are still young. Good luck
Comment by ki1abyte: honestly bro, at this point in the semester id say just withdraw from all your classes (aka the semester). once you withdraw from the semester you can then get therapy from the school or just find resources to help you get back in the right headspace. most professor by this point would not just let someone submit all their work to get a good grade, it's just not possible. and also taking the Fs would be the worst option because the Fs WILL stay on your transcript, and you can only grade swap 4 classes. hope you get better tho bro ive been thru the same and wish i did the withdrawal option.
Comment by BeachgirlNJ0613: No! Do not just take the Fs. It's harder to deal with them after the fact than before. I mean, you can retake the courses and replace the grades, but you can only do that for 4 classes. Try to withdraw. Can you go see a doctor and get a medical excuse? You can also take summer classes which are easier because you do one at a time. There are 2 "semesters" in the summer. It's hard to get behind when you go to only one class per day. You can take a summer course at any state school near your home and Rutgers accepts the credits. That way, you can catch up more easily. But a significant percentage of students do not graduate in 4 years. At Rutgers NB it's kinda high at around 70%, but at Newark and Camden its much lower. You can fix this, but try to do it now. Keep the faith. Good luck.
Comment by Givemeurto3s: I feel you, last sem I failed 3/6 of mine. I took the F’s and am retaking them now. Don’t think you are emotional, I had the same kind of thing happen to me last semester too, I took some time over winter break to think if I was still interested in going into my field. And if I felt it was obtainable and still right for me. I think doing that really helped me realize and regain a bit of that drive. Don’t be discouraged tho
Comment by RepentantDayZBandit: This sounds like a situation I was in a few years ago where I ended up with 4/4 Fs because I gave up halfway through the semester. My advice would be to salvage what you can. For the classes you have any hope of passing you should put all your effort towards those so you can at least pass some of them. You probably won’t be able to pass all of them from the sound of it so just try to be strategic and salvage some of them. 

It sounds like you’re not in the right headspace to be in college right now and you should seriously consider taking a semester or two off to really reflect on what your goals with school are and if you’re ready to commit to them. I know there can be a lot of pressure to just continue on by friends and family but the mature decision might be to take a break and recuperate.

Only other thing I would add is that one really bad semester feels like the end of the world in the moment but it’s not nearly as big of a deal as you think it is. Your situation is a lot more common than you think. Graduating a year or two later than your peers is meaningless in the long run. Just take ownership of what happened and try to grow from it.
Comment by Legitimate-Rhubarb91: I failed three semesters ina row youll be chillin in life 🤣
Comment by Full-Personality2895: It’s not about the classes at this point, you need to fix yourself and lack of discipline. Even if you pressed a button and could magically make your Fs into As the actual problem is clear. You need to replace whoever you associate with people who actually care about you because whoever your surrounded by failed you and are probably losers themselves.
Comment by Accomplished-Let3639: Talk to the Dean of Students and see if you can take a temporary grade and finish your work in the summer
Comment by Any_Dragonfruit_7669: Simple as this: You lock tf in for the rest of the semester and beg every professor for a change to make up wtv u missed (keep excuses as a last resort, dont give details on why you missed what you missed).

You could stilll fail, but that's literally your only option,
Comment by WHT_QM: Retroactive withdrawal from the semester is likely better, not enough time to "lock in"
Comment by goodgreif_11: If it makes you feel better im failing 2/4 classes because those two classes are the same prof 🙃
Comment by superadaptoid47: Go talk to the instructor in person . Explain that you understood that you made a mistake, you've learned your lesson , and you want a fresh start. Suggest that you want to leave the course and come back and try it again. Ask if it's okay to receive a temporary grade and attend the class the next time it's offered , repeat all the assignments, and have the temporary grade replaced with whatever you earn when you retake the class. If they agree, there won't be an F on your transcript. The temporary grade will be replaced with whatever grade you earn later, you won't have to re-register for the course and pay again, and the instructor might be satisfied that you will learn all the material and do all the work the next time they offer the class. The worst they can do is say no.
Comment by Plenty-Discussion206: experienced the same thing senior year of hs. i ended up dropping out for 3 semesters. take a break , if you paid insurance u can take this semester off and get Ws for everything and get ur money back. goodluck it gets better i promise
Comment by jrsygirlsdontpumpgas: Do you have a mental health doctor… sounds like you are struggling… you could get a medical withdrawal…

Comment by Original_Airline_323: You chose not to participate because you “lacked motivation,” but that’s something most students deal with at some point. It doesn’t make you an exception. If someone can fail most of their classes, miss the withdrawal deadline, and still receive Ws instead of Fs, it raises a fairness issue. What message does that send to students who stayed engaged all semester or made the responsible choice to withdraw on time? Take the Fs you deserve, tough love. This path will ensure you won’t allow anything like this to happen again.
Comment by That-Lingonberry-779: College is useless and just puts you in serious debt after you graduate!  Find something you’re passionate about and just try to find a job in that area.
